item.title: Incarico post-doc: Brand Experience and Consumer Well-being in Digital Environments: Branding Strategies for Shared Value Creation (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-14 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/ECON-07 Economia e gestione delle imprese

This research lies at the intersection of brand strategy and consumer behavior in digital experiential contexts, aiming to investigate how brands can pursue their strategic objectives by fully leveraging technological potential while simultaneously protecting and enhancing consumer well-being. By employing mixed (qualitative and quantitative) methodological approaches, the project aims to develop a framework to support the planning of branding strategies in digital environments, exploring the conditions that allow brand goals to be reconciled with the psychological well-being of the consumer.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Models and Methods for Unsupervised Classification of Functional Data with Applications to Dynamic Survival Prediction via Landmarking (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/STAT-01 Statistica

The aim of this project is to propose and develop new methods and models for the unsupervised classification of functional data. These methods will also leverage the functional nature of routinely collected longitudinal patient data to provide more accurate prognostic information for dynamic survival models. Techniques from functional clustering will be extended to account for the sparse and irregular nature of longitudinal data. The extracted information on heterogeneous biomarkers is then integrated into survival models that dynamically estimate survival curves within a landmarking framework. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Multi-source data and non-probability samples (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/STAT-01 Statistica

The statistical literature investigates estimators based on non-probability samples under a set of highly restrictive “standard” conditions, which are rarely met in real-world applications. The project aims to develop new estimators and new methods for assessing sampling error when these standard conditions do not hold. The postdoctoral researcher’s work will involve both theoretical research, focusing on the properties—particularly the asymptotic properties—of the proposed estimators, and simulation-based investigations. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in SMEs: Digital Transformation, Governance, and Competitiveness (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-01 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/ECON-07 Economia e gestione delle imprese

The research activity will focus on the study of innovation and entrepreneurship processes in SMEs, with particular emphasis on the impact of digital technologies on organizational and governance models. Specific topics for in-depth analysis may include competitiveness, adaptability, sustainability, risk management, and value creation. Both theoretical and empirical approaches—utilizing quantitative and qualitative methodologies—will be valued, consistent with the project's objectives and key research trends in management studies.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Health, living standards and regional inequalities in Italy. A long-term historical perspective (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-30 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/STEC-01 Storia dell'economia

Understanding why some populations live longer and in better health than others is one of the most significant issues of our time. The relationship between income and health — summarised by the so-called Preston Curve (Preston, 1975) — lies at the heart of crucial debates: to what extent does economic growth automatically lead to improvements in life expectancy? And to what extent can the spread of medical knowledge, hygiene practices and public intervention improve health regardless of income? The answer to these questions has direct implications for developing countries today: if medical knowledge and the transfer of low-cost healthcare technology have historically contributed as much —…
